message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he mentioned in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost can be deducted from your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of their stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party where he was also present. We were being polite, and then he asked how the move-out process went. I told him it was good, and naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games. I told him that I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now, he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things: 1. **Communication**: Did I make a reasonable effort to contact him about his stuff? 2. **Intentions**: Was my intention to help him by selling his games, or was it to benefit myself? 3. **Legal Standing**: Is there any legal obligation I had to fulfill regarding his property? 4. **Moral Perspective**: Even if it's legal, is there a moral issue with selling someone else's stuff without their consent? 5. **Consequences**: How has this affected our relationship, and is that a factor in determining if I'm the asshole? Let me break this down step by step. First, communication. I tried to contact him for two weeks via text and email. That seems like a reasonable effort. I can't force him to respond, so after that, I had to make a decision. Next, intentions. I sold his games to avoid the landlord deducting money from my deposit for having to remove his stuff. It was a practical decision to prevent financial loss. However, by selling his games, I also benefited financially by getting $600. So, my intention was twofold: to protect my financial interest and to gain some money. Legally, I checked, and there's nothing wrong with what I did. The landlord can deduct for removal costs, and selling the games seems to be a way to mitigate that loss. So, legally, I'm in the clear. Now, morally, is there an issue? I sold his stuff without his consent. Even though I tried to contact him, he didn't respond. In some cultures or moral frameworks, using someone else's property without their explicit consent, even if it's for their benefit, can be seen as wrong. Also, the consequence is that he's upset and calling me an asshole. Relationships matter, and if this action has damaged our relationship, that's a factor to consider. So, putting it all together, while legally I'm not in the wrong, morally, there's a gray area. I used his property without his consent, even if it was for what I perceived as a good reason. Additionally, the fact that I gained financially from selling his games might make it seem like I'm exploiting the situation, even if that wasn't my intention. In conclusion, while I might not be legally in the wrong, there's a moral aspect to consider.
